The menu leaves out all, region and avoid-region: css-compat.json keeps them only because BCD does not track them and the browser syntax lists them, but they break through nested fragmentation contexts and CSS Regions, which no browser implements and the editor never creates. avoid, avoid-page and avoid-column are left out too: BCD notes for Firefox and Safari that the value is recognized but has no effect (break-before.avoid: firefox and safari false; avoid-page and avoid-column: firefox false), so a page exported with it would break where the editor promised it would not; break-inside offers avoid because all three act on it there.

omits.reason: A layer edit never touches the colour under the layers: Pager wrote the background shorthand for a gradient and erased background-color (spec gradient-editor, problem 1). The colour has its own field.

subsets.reason: The menu offers the transitions a page usually takes; any other shorthand is typed and read as the longhands it writes.

storedWhole.reason: BCD records animation-delay-start and animation-delay-end (CSS Animations 2) with no browser entry: every browser implements animation-delay itself, and no browser implements the longhands, so the timeline's Delay field stores it whole.
BCD has no entry for box-shadow-color, box-shadow-offset, box-shadow-blur, box-shadow-spread or box-shadow-position: no browser implements the longhands, every browser implements box-shadow.
BCD has no entry for text-align-all: browsers implement text-align itself. text-align-last, which every browser implements, is not edited, so text-align keeps one writer.

Safari lacks baseline-source, and BCD records the CSS Inline 3 values of vertical-align (first, last, center, alphabetic, central...) only in Firefox: Chrome and Safari implement vertical-align as the CSS 2 property, not as the shorthand of alignment-baseline, baseline-shift and baseline-source, so a composite of those longhands would not do what vertical-align does there.

syntaxFallbacks.reason: The Fill and Stroke 3 draft's <paint> no longer lists <color>, although every browser accepts a colour (the SVG shape default fill: #dbe7ff); the browser syntax still has it.

CSS Overflow 4, 5.1.1 Legacy compatibility: the legacy line clamp only takes effect when display is -webkit-box or -webkit-inline-box. webref defines no such display value and BCD does not track it; the browser syntax (MDN) has it, and the spec section is the evidence for the recipe.
